title: Beef and barley pot with Brussels sprouts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Mince, barley, stock, tomato purée and Worcestershire sauce are all things a grandparent would have kept in the kitchen.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded casserole and a wooden spoon, and the techniques are basic browning and simmering.

works.reason: 500g mince, 250g barley and 400g sprouts make four good portions. 1.2 litres of stock over 45 covered minutes will cook the barley through to a loose, stew-like pot, and halved sprouts are tender in 10 minutes.

honest_times.reason: 20 minutes of prep covers the chopping plus browning and softening, with the sprouts halved while the barley simmers. The 45-minute cook matches the 35 plus 10 minutes of simmering.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme and Worcestershire, appears in the steps, and nothing else is used apart from the stock.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming beef and barley pot suits early November, and 400g of sprouts makes them the main vegetable rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling one-pot meal of beef, whole grain and plenty of vegetables that a family would happily eat again.
